title: U.S. House · Nevada's 4th District
area: North Las Vegas and a broad swath of rural central and southern Nevada, stretching from the Las Vegas Valley to Pahrump and the state's rural counties.

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled after incumbent Steven Horsford (D) faced no primary challenger and advanced automatically. Cody Whipple won the Republican primary. Independent American Party candidate Russell Best and no-party candidate William Johnson also qualified for the general-election ballot; Gary Steele (No Political Party) withdrew or was disqualified.

summary.text: Steven Horsford is the Democratic incumbent in Nevada's 4th District, serving since 2019 and previously from 2013 to 2015. A Las Vegas native, he was a Nevada state senator and Senate Majority Leader and led the Culinary Training Academy of Las Vegas before entering Congress. He sits on the Ways and Means Committee and chaired the Congressional Black Caucus from 2023 to 2025.

background.text: Born and raised in Las Vegas; his official biography says his mother immigrated to the United States and that he lost his father when he was 19.
Graduated from Clark High School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Nevada, Reno.

Worked at the Las Vegas marketing and consulting firm R&R Partners beginning in 1996, according to Wikipedia, and was executive director of the Culinary Training Academy of Las Vegas, which his official biography describes as the largest job training program in Nevada.

Served in the Nevada State Senate from 2004 to 2012, including as Majority Leader from 2009 to 2012; his official biography describes him as the first African American Majority Leader of the Nevada State Senate.
Won Nevada's 4th District in 2012 (50.1% to 42.1% over Danny Tarkanian) and served one term, then lost re-election in 2014 to Cresent Hardy, 48.5% to 45.8%.

After leaving Congress, he started a small business; his official biography cites a workforce development program for young people in North Las Vegas with Intel and a food recovery program with Three Square. Wikipedia reports he rejoined R&R Partners.

Elected again to the open 4th District seat in 2018; serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Health and Social Security subcommittees) for 2025-2026, and earlier served on committees including Financial Services, Armed Services, Budget, and Natural Resources.
Chaired the Congressional Black Caucus from January 2023 to January 2025.
His official biography says he has three children.

positions.summary: His official House website states he is fighting for comprehensive immigration reform and is an original co-sponsor of the American Dream and Promise Act, which would create a path to citizenship for "Dreamers" and protect Temporary Protected Status and Deferred Enforced Departure recipients from removal.
positions.quote: Congressman Horsford is an original co-sponsor of the American Dream and Promise Act, a landmark bill that will create a path to citizenship for dreamers and protect Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders, and Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) recipients from being forced to leave the country they love.

summary.text: Cody Whipple is the Republican nominee in Nevada's 4th District; he won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 61.8% of the vote. A fourth-generation Nevadan, he is a rancher and the owner of a communications-equipment business. His campaign website says he is running on lowering the cost of living, supporting small businesses, improving public safety, and parental control of education.

background.text: Born and raised in Hiko, Nevada, in Lincoln County, on his family's cattle ranch; his father died of cancer when he was young, leaving his mother to raise five children, according to his campaign website.
Graduated from Pahranagat Valley High School in 1992 and played football at Virginia Tech on a scholarship.
Earned a degree in animal science from Virginia Tech, where he met his wife, Dana; the couple worked in Virginia for a few years before returning to Nevada and have three daughters.

Worked in sales for McIntosh Communications before founding Rebel Communications in 2005, a company that services and programs radio equipment for emergency vehicles, school districts, and businesses.
Manages the family ranch in Hiko and, according to his campaign website, has coached young athletes; he and his family have lived in both Las Vegas and Hiko.
Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary, defeating Ronda Kennedy and Anthony Snowden; this is his first run for the seat, and he has run without national political consultants.

summary.text: Russell Best is the Independent American Party candidate in Nevada's 4th District. A mortgage company owner and Navy veteran by Ballotpedia's account, he has run for Congress and governor in several earlier elections as an Independent American candidate.

background.text: Born in Texas; according to Ballotpedia, he joined the Navy as a storekeeper and was honorably discharged for medical reasons.

After graduating from Moorepark College (as Ballotpedia spells it), worked for companies including Gulf Oil, Taco Bell, and Meritor Mortgage, and owns and operates an independent mortgage company in northern Nevada.

Independent American Party candidate for U.S. House in Nevada's 2nd District in 2012 (2.1%) and 2022 (1.4%), for Nevada's 4th District in 2014 (2.6%), and for Governor of Nevada in 2018 (1.0%); also on the 2024 general-election ballot in the 4th District.

summary.text: William Johnson is a no-party candidate on the November general-election ballot for U.S. House Nevada District 4. Ballotpedia lists no biography, campaign website, or earlier campaigns for him.

sources.title: Cody Whipple does things 'my way.' Can the small-town rancher flip Nevada's bluest House seat?

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Horsford are added separately by script. Cody Whipple's campaign website and a Nevada Independent profile were used for his biography. No campaign website, public statements, or Candidate Connection survey were found for Russell Best or William Johnson, and no biographical information about Johnson was found.
